Name: Mercedes R. Lackey
Question: Since a fictional world is a representation of a possibility, are the scenarios presented (the emotions, actions and interactions of the fictional characters), true, factual and genuine within that possibility (alternative reality)?
Answer: Maybe. But you’d better give justification for your decisions to the reader or they’ll toss the book across the room and never read you again.

Name: Mercedes R. Lackey
Question: If digitally “resurrecting” James Dean through CGI in Finding Jack proves to be a far better breakthrough than anyone expects it to be, will this inspire the film industry to “revive” more actors in film and animation?
Answer: The film industry is salivating at the thought that they can use disposable stand-ins and then paint the image of box office stars over the top of them. They are also salivating at the idea that CGI Replicants will eventually (sooner rather than later) become so convicing and cheap that they’ll never need to hire a star again.

Name: Mercedes R. Lackey
Question: My incarcerated uncle wrote several books and short stories. Where can I post one of his short stories that possible publishers or people that can assist with getting them published can read it?
Answer: Unfortunately there is a myth going around that publishers and agents are reading works self-published online in order to find new writers. This is a myth, and is completely untrue. They are already drowning in unsolicited submissions, and have no time to go surfing through self-published stuff online. If you want to help him, then the best thing you can do for him is to pick out the best of his books and get a professional editor to give it a full edit. Then he needs to revise and rewrite his book according to the professional editor’s suggestions, and this will probably take at least five or six rewrites. Once he’s done with that, you can take the next steps.

Name: Mercedes R. Lackey
Question: What did Harris know of Joe's dementia, and when did she know it?
Answer: People bandy the word “dementia” around a lot. Dementia is a measurable mental condition. It often involves halucinations. Joe Biden does not have it. My mother in law, rest her, had it. I know exactly what it looks like. It looks nothing like anything Joe Biden does. What Joe Biden has is plain old age. The older you get, the easier it is to get worn out. The older you get, the harder it is to remember things—as in, things that would come instantly to you now take five or ten minutes to remember. The older you get, the more time you need to make a decision. That’s what my late father looked like, and that’s what Joe Biden looks like. Short form, in my opinion, Joe just “couldn’t keep up.” He understands exactly what is going on, but he can’t react to it anymore as fast as he used to. And in today’s political climate, if you can’t react fast, you’d better get out of the way and let those who can take over. Which is what he did. And if he had had dementia, he never would have stepped aside, because people with dementia have no idea that they aren’t as fast as they used to be.

Name: Mercedes R. Lackey
Question: How would you summarize a technique for creating a character?
Answer: I decide the kind of person or creature that fits the needs of the skeletal story. Then I work out their character traits, good and bad, weaknesses and strengths. And most of all, I figure out what their problem is going to be, because solving that problem and having them come out the better for their struggles in the end is what makes a satisfying story.

Name: Mercedes R. Lackey
Question: How do you write a “big bad” villain well?
Answer: Don’t make him evil “just because” he is evil. He needs motivation. And it needs to be an understandable motivation.

Question: Is there a difference between a fanfiction and a web serial novel?
Answer: Fanfiction uses someone else’s setting, worldbuilding, and often characters. A web serial novel uses your own setting, worldbuilding and characters. If you try to make money with fanfiction, you will be sued by the person whose work you used. You can try to make money with a web serial novel without being sued by anyone.
